\chapter{Babies}
\label{ch:ar-babies}
\hlchaptermodality{530}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say that a woman is pregnant, talk about a cradle, and say that a mother breastfed, weaned or brought up a child.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 530: I can say that a woman is pregnant, talk about a cradle, and say that a mother breastfed, weaned or brought up a child.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حامل} (ḥāmil)}{حامل (ḥāmil)}]{\ar{حامل} (ḥāmil) — pregnant}

\label{lesson:AR-C530-hamil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a brother-in-law, then the Arabic for a marriage break-up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حامل}}
\textbf{\ar{حامل}} — \emph{ḥāmil} — \textquotedblleft{}pregnant\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{زوجة} \ar{أخي} \ar{حامل} \ar{بطفلها} \ar{الأول}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{zawjat akhī ḥāmil bi-ṭiflihā al-awwal.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother's wife is pregnant with her first child.
\end{quote}

It has no feminine ending, since only a woman is \ar{حامل}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حامل}} (\emph{ḥāmil}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-m-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to carry\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Ḥamala, to carry, which you know, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥāmil}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥāmil}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zawjat akhī ḥāmil bi-ṭiflihā al-awwal.} — My brother's wife is pregnant with her first child.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a brother-in-law, then the Arabic for a marriage break-up, then say \emph{ḥāmil} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{حامل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Pregnant\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مهد} (mahd)}{مهد (mahd)}]{\ar{مهد} (mahd) — a cradle}

\label{lesson:AR-C530-mahd}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a marriage break-up, then the Arabic for pregnant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مهد}}
\textbf{\ar{مهد}} — \emph{mahd} — \textquotedblleft{}a cradle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نام} \ar{الطفل} \ar{في} \ar{المهد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nāma aṭ-ṭifl fī al-mahd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The baby slept in the cradle.
\end{quote}

\ar{من} \ar{المهد} is from the cradle, from early childhood.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مهد}} (\emph{mahd}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{m-h-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to smooth, to spread out\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A mahd is a bed made smooth for a child.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mahd}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mahd}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nāma aṭ-ṭifl fī al-mahd.} — The baby slept in the cradle.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a marriage break-up, then the Arabic for pregnant, then say \emph{mahd} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مهد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A cradle\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أرضع} (arḍaʿa)}{أرضع (arḍaʿa)}]{\ar{أرضع} (arḍaʿa) — to breastfeed}

\label{lesson:AR-C530-ardaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for pregnant, then the Arabic for a cradle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أرضع}}
\textbf{\ar{أرضع}} — \emph{arḍaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to breastfeed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أرضعت} \ar{الأم} \ar{طفلها} \ar{في} \ar{الصباح}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{arḍaʿat al-umm ṭiflahā fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mother fed her baby in the morning.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يرضع}, \emph{yurḍiʿ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أرضع}} (\emph{arḍaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-ḍ-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to suck the breast\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form IV arḍaʿa is to give the breast.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arḍaʿa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arḍaʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arḍaʿat al-umm ṭiflahā fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ.} — The mother fed her baby in the morning.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for pregnant, then the Arabic for a cradle, then say \emph{arḍaʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أرضع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To breastfeed\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فطم} (faṭama)}{فطم (faṭama)}]{\ar{فطم} (faṭama) — to wean}

\label{lesson:AR-C530-fatama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a cradle, then the Arabic for to breastfeed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فطم}}
\textbf{\ar{فطم}} — \emph{faṭama} — \textquotedblleft{}to wean\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{فطمت} \ar{أختي} \ar{ابنها} \ar{بعد} \ar{سنتين}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{faṭamat ukhtī ibnahā baʿda sanatayn.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister weaned her son after two years.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يفطم}, \emph{yafṭim}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فطم}} (\emph{faṭama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-ṭ-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to cut off\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives faṭama, aor. yafṭimu, as to cut off: weaning cuts the child off the breast.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{faṭama}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{faṭama}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{faṭamat ukhtī ibnahā baʿda sanatayn.} — My sister weaned her son after two years.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a cradle, then the Arabic for to breastfeed, then say \emph{faṭama} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ربى} (rabbā)}{ربى (rabbā)}]{\ar{ربى} (rabbā) — to bring up}

\label{lesson:AR-C530-rabba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to breastfeed, then the Arabic for to wean.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ربى}}
\textbf{\ar{ربى}} — \emph{rabbā} — \textquotedblleft{}to bring up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ربت} \ar{أمي} \ar{خمسة} \ar{أولاد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rabbat ummī khamsat awlād.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother brought up five children.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يربي}, \emph{yurabbī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ربى}} (\emph{rabbā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-b-w}, \textquotedblleft{}to grow, to increase\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form II rabbā is to make a child grow.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}
